terms.definition_en: The capability of computer systems to perform tasks that require human intelligence, such as learning from patterns and making decisions.
A step-by-step procedure or formula for solving a problem or accomplishing a task.
The ability to identify recurring structures or regularities in data.
A subset of AI where systems learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed.
A computing system inspired by biological neural networks that constitute animal brains.
A subset of machine learning using multiple layers of artificial neural networks.
The dataset used to train a machine learning model to recognize patterns.
A mathematical representation of learned patterns from training data.
AI systems that can create new, original content such as text, images, or code.
A neural network model trained on massive amounts of text data to understand and generate human language.
A neural network architecture that uses attention mechanisms to process sequences of data.
A small unit of text, often a word or part of a word, that an AI model processes.
An input or instruction given to an AI model to generate a desired output.
A technique that retrieves relevant information from a database and uses it to enhance AI-generated responses.
When an AI model generates incorrect or fabricated information.
Numerical representations of words or concepts that capture their semantic meaning.
A technique that allows neural networks to focus on the most relevant parts of input data.
Learnable variables in a neural network that are adjusted during training.
Complete passes through the entire training dataset during model training.
A mathematical function that measures how far a model's predictions are from the actual data.
